report.source_text: However, at this time the patient was noted to have a large semi-solid anterior vaginal wall mass that was felt to be separate from the urethra. Due to its size and taut cystic nature, a transvaginal ultrasound was performed to characterize the mass. The differential diagnoses at this time included vaginal cyst, vaginal fibroid, or vaginal malignancy. The ultra-sound report documented a solid septated mass distending the anterior vaginal wall and distorting the endocervical canal. The mass was 5×5×4.2 cm, the rim of the mass was vascular, and the mass was septated (Figure 1). The etiology of the mass was uncertain.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 25-year-old primigravida with chronic hypertension, hidradenitis suppurativa, and morbid obesity presented for initial prenatal visit at 10 weeks 3 days gestation with normal pelvic examination. She had a prior UTI at 6 weeks gestation with moderate RBCs and positive leukocyte esterase. During pregnancy, she developed dysuria at 27 weeks with hematuria on dipstick and mixed bacterial flora on urine culture. Microscopic hematuria was documented on multiple antenatal visits. At 38 weeks 4 days gestation, a large anterior vaginal wall mass measuring 5×5×4.2 cm was identified on transvaginal ultrasound, described as a solid septated mass distending the anterior vaginal wall with a vascular rim and uncertain etiology. CT scan of the abdomen and pelvis was performed, which identified an anterior vaginal wall mass measuring 2×4×2 cm, confirming the diagnosis of urethral diverticulum.
